name: IN-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean anchors the seat firmly in Republican hands
Houchin's roughly 11-to-1 fundraising edge ($2.2M raised vs. $195K for Meyer)
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 97 percent
No public polling or expert ratings; challenger lacks outside spending support
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Houchin's dominant fundraising, and market pricing near 97 percent for the GOP all point the same direction, and even a national environment that has favored Democrats this cycle cannot plausibly close a gap that large for an underfunded challenger.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or polling showing an unusually strong national environment could narrow the margin, though the structural deficit would remain steep.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 9th District sits in the Republican-leaning southern part of the state, where the partisan baseline favors the GOP by roughly fifteen points. Representative Erin Houchin is seeking re-election with a large financial edge, having raised about $2.2 million and holding more than $900,000 on hand. Democrat Brad Meyer has raised under $200,000, and a Libertarian candidate adds a minor third option on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, candidate resources, and betting markets, which price a Republican win near 97 percent. Even allowing for a national environment that has at times favored Democrats this cycle, the combination of incumbency, geography, and money leaves Meyer with a very narrow path. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with low odds of a competitive finish.
